advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guarantee unique discovery unit_ids (de-dupe or disambiguate) before building DiscoveryStagePlan so a prompt/id collision cannot raise ValueError and abort the whole review.
evidence: batch_runner.py:184 `return str(logical) if isinstance(logical, str) and logical else str(crit.get("prompt"))`
batch_runner.py:118-121 builds `units = tuple(self._unit_plan(crit, model) ...)` then `DiscoveryStagePlan(units=units, ...)`
discovery.py:139-143 `def __post_init__(self): ... _validate_topology(self.units)`
discovery.py:277-279 `if len(ids) != len(set(ids)): ... raise ValueError(f"duplicate unit_id(s) in stage plan: {dupes}")`
Pre-cutover code (removed) iterated `for crit in active_criteria:` running each entry with no de-dup/collision constraint.
advisory.finding: A duplicate discovery unit_id aborts the entire review with an uncaught ValueError. `_unit_id` falls back to the prompt string, and `DiscoveryStagePlan.__post_init__` calls `_validate_topology`, which raises `ValueError("duplicate unit_id(s)...")` if any two included criteria resolve to the same unit_id (e.g. two `req.criteria` entries sharing a prompt with no distinct criterion_id, or a built-in overlay colliding with a project criterion's prompt-derived id). The pre-cutover loop simply ran each entry, so this is a new hard-failure edge.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire the new helpers (changed_files into the runner, snapshot into run_detectors/DET consumer, round_a_selection/partial_failure_verdict/shadow_compare, and discovery_trace into the verdict/sidecar) into the production dispatch path, or clearly mark them as staged and out of the live flow.
evidence: gate_dispatch.py:514-523 constructs `CodeReviewBatchRunner(context=..., context_overrides=..., project_criteria=..., project_criteria_root=...)` with no `changed_files=` argument
batch_runner.py:297 `if self._changed_files and not self._project_applies(logical_id, repo_root):` — guard is inert when changed_files is empty (the prod default)
search for `det_criteria_from_snapshot`, `round_a_selection`, `partial_failure_verdict`, `shadow_compare`, `discovery_trace_from_journal` returns only tests/* callers besides their definitions
detectors.py:156-157 prod consumer `apply_failclosed` still calls `run_security_detectors(...)` (no snapshot) and `registry.det_criteria()`
advisory.finding: The advertised RP-06 S3 'cutover' features are not wired into the production dispatch path — only exercised by tests. gate_dispatch constructs CodeReviewBatchRunner WITHOUT `changed_files=`, so the runner's new project-applicability gate (`if self._changed_files and not self._project_applies(...)`) never fires in production; and `det_criteria_from_snapshot`, `run_detectors(snapshot=...)`, `registry.round_a_selection`, `workflow_ops.partial_failure_verdict`, `workflow_ops.shadow_compare`, and `sidecar.discovery_trace_from_journal` have no production callers.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Connect batch_plan['discovery_trace'] into verdict['discovery_trace'] (via discovery_trace_from_journal) so the sidecar journal branch is actually reachable, or remove the dead branch.
evidence: sidecar.py:130-134 `trace = verdict.get("discovery_trace")` then `if trace: payload["discovery_trace"] = trace`
search for `discovery_trace` shows it set only on `plan["discovery_trace"]` (batch_plan) in batch_runner.py, never on any `verdict` dict
`discovery_trace_from_journal` (sidecar.py:61) is called only in tests/unit/test_code_review_discovery.py
advisory.finding: The sidecar's discovery-trace propagation branch is dead: `_verdict_payload` copies `verdict.get("discovery_trace")` into the payload, but no code ever sets `verdict["discovery_trace"]`. The trace is written to `batch_plan["discovery_trace"]` and extracted by `discovery_trace_from_journal`, which itself has no production caller, so the journal never reaches the sidecar payload.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a build_payload test asserting `discovery_trace` is present on the payload when the verdict carries a truthy trace, and absent (payload unchanged) when it is missing/empty.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:132-134: `trace = verdict.get("discovery_trace")` / `if trace:` / `payload["discovery_trace"] = trace`

search across tests: every `discovery_trace` test hit references `batch_plan["discovery_trace"]` or `discovery_trace_from_journal`; none feeds a verdict with `discovery_trace` to `sidecar.build_payload` and asserts the persisted payload key
The diff comment claims 'absent otherwise, so existing payloads stay byte-identical' — this parity/absence claim has no asserting test.
advisory.finding: sidecar.build_payload's new discovery_trace emission is untested: no test asserts the top-level `discovery_trace` key is carried when verdict.get('discovery_trace') is truthy, nor that it is omitted (payload stays byte-identical) when absent/empty.
advisory.suggested_fix: Two cases over sidecar.build_payload: verdict with `discovery_trace=[{...}]` -> `payload['discovery_trace'] == [...]`; verdict without it -> `'discovery_trace' not in payload`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a run_detectors(snapshot=...) test asserting a snapshot-activated project DET criterion selects/runs its detector, distinct from the registry.det_criteria() default path.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:96-98: `det_map = (det_criteria_from_snapshot(snapshot) if snapshot is not None else registry.det_criteria())`

search `run_detectors`: existing callers in tests (test_code_review_conflict_markers, test_code_review_public_exposure, test_code_review_ws5, test_det_invariants) all call `run_detectors(changed_files=..., repo_root=...)` with no `snapshot=` argument
The new tests (test_det_invariants.py, test_code_review_discovery.py) only assert on `det_criteria_from_snapshot(snap)` directly, never driving it through run_detectors.
advisory.finding: run_detectors' new `snapshot=` parameter is untested at the run_detectors boundary. Tests exercise det_criteria_from_snapshot directly but never call run_detectors(snapshot=...), so the new branch selecting the snapshot-derived det_map (vs registry.det_criteria()) and its effect on detector slicing/bucketing is not covered.
advisory.suggested_fix: Build a repo with an activated project DET, compile a snapshot, call run_detectors(changed_files=[...], repo_root=..., snapshot=snap) and assert the project detector's bucket appears in the result.
